english.title: Remove imported goods before examination with intent to defraud / evade a prohibition / restriction
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to

(A)_[defraud His Majesty of duty chargeable on]_
(B)_[evade the prohibition or restriction, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITION OR RESTRICTION..), on the importation of]_

goods, namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS..), removed those goods from customs and excise charge before they had been examined by an officer having power to do so under the Customs and Excise Act 1979
english.legislation: Contrary to section 159(6) and (7) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

english.notes: Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £20,000 or three times the value of the goods involved, whichever is the greater.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions
20 years
